title: Zero entries propagate through all spectral-sequence pages
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and let $(E_r^{p,q},d_r)_{r\ge2}$ be a cohomological spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence] indexed by $(p,q)\in\mathbb Z^2$, with $d_r:E_r^{p,q}\to E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$ and specified isomorphisms from the homology of page $r$ to page $r+1$. For every $s\ge2$, every $(p,q)\in\mathbb Z^2$, and every $r\ge s$, if $E_s^{p,q}$ is a zero object, then $E_r^{p,q}$ is a zero object. Consequently, if $E_2^{p,q}=0$ whenever $p<0$ or $q<0$, and also $E_2^{p,q}=0$ whenever $q>0$, then $E_r^{p,q}=0$ whenever $p<0$ or $q\ne0$, for every $r\ge2$. In particular every eventually stationary term in any positive row is zero.

source.place: Tag 0BDV (lemma-relate-boundedness), proof hint: a zero entry stays zero on every later page; Tag 011N (definition-spectral-sequence), page homology. This states the propagation argument of the row-collapse proof, without an abutment or edge map.

proof.text: Fix $t\ge2$ and $(p,q)\in\mathbb Z^2$. The page differentials give the short complex $S=(E_t^{p-t,q+t-1}\xrightarrow{d_t}E_t^{p,q}\xrightarrow{d_t}E_t^{p+t,q-t+1})$: the composite is zero because page $t$ is a complex [def-sp-spectral-sequence]. If $E_t^{p,q}$ is a zero object, the first assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-short-complex-zero-homology] says $H(S)$ is a zero object. The specified page isomorphism $\phi:H(S)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{t+1}^{p,q}$ then makes $E_{t+1}^{p,q}$ a zero object: for any object $T$, composition with $\phi$ and $\phi^{-1}$ gives bijections on both Hom sets, so their uniqueness for $H(S)$ gives uniqueness for $E_{t+1}^{p,q}$.

source.place: Tag 011N (definition-spectral-sequence), page homology; Tag 0BDV (lemma-relate-boundedness), proof hint.

proof.text: Fix $s\ge2$ and $(p,q)$ with $E_s^{p,q}$ a zero object. Induct on $k\in\mathbb N$ to show that $E_{s+k}^{p,q}$ is a zero object. At $k=0$ this is the hypothesis. For the successor, use Step 1 with $t=s+k\ge2$ and the induction hypothesis, obtaining $E_{s+k+1}^{p,q}=0$. Given any integer $r\ge s$, the nonnegative integer $r-s$ equals some $k\in\mathbb N$ and $r=s+k$, proving the first assertion.

source.place: Tag 0BDV (lemma-relate-boundedness), proof hint, expanded as induction on the page difference.

proof.text: Under the two page-two vanishing hypotheses, fix $(p,q)$ with $p<0$ or $q\ne0$. If $p<0$ or $q<0$, the first hypothesis gives $E_2^{p,q}=0$. In the remaining case $q\ne0$ and $q\ge0$, hence $q>0$, so the second hypothesis gives the same vanishing. Step 2 with $s=2$ yields $E_r^{p,q}=0$ for every $r\ge2$. In particular for $q>0$ every term is zero, so any eventually stationary value, represented by any sufficiently late page term, is a zero object.

lean.statement: theorem spectral_page_zero_propagation {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (E : E₂CohomologicalSpectralSequence C) : (∀ (s : ℤ) (hs : 2 ≤ s) (p q r : ℤ) (hsr : s ≤ r), IsZero ((E.page s hs).X (p, q)) → IsZero ((E.page r (le_trans hs hsr)).X (p, q))) ∧ ((∀ p q : ℤ, p < 0 ∨ q < 0 → IsZero ((E.page 2).X (p, q))) → (∀ p q : ℤ, 0 < q → IsZero ((E.page 2).X (p, q))) → (∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (p q : ℤ), p < 0 ∨ q ≠ 0 → IsZero ((E.page r hr).X (p, q))) ∧ ∀ p q : ℤ, 0 < q → ∀ Z : C, (∃ (R : ℤ) (hR : 2 ≤ R), ∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : R ≤ r), Nonempty ((E.page r (le_trans hR hr)).X (p, q) ≅ Z)) → IsZero Z)
